content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge treats a single verse's two possible readings as making the matter UNDERDETERMINED.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.\" I weighed whether a single verse admitting two readings may be UNDERDETERMINED, versus whether such a verse is not open and both senses stand so it cannot ground UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"The judge's stated reason relies on Matthew 1:16 admitting two readings, which K-S2 forbids as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED."}
